sentences.text: Appearance:
Shri Amar Singh Rathore - Advocate for the applicant.
Shri Virendra Khadav - G.A. appearing on behalf of Advo  ORDER 1.
They are heard.
Perused the case diary / challan papers.

2. This is the first bail application filed by the applicant under Section 483 of BNSS, 2023 / 439 of Criminal Procedure Code, 1973, as he / she is implicated in connection with Crime No.345/2025 registered at Police Station Lasudiya, Indore (MP) for offence punishable under Section 420, 465,
467, 468, 471, 120-B of Indian Penal Code, 1860.
The applicant is lodged in jail since 13/06/2025.
3. Allegation against the applicant is of fraud and illegal occupation of the complainant's land.

4. Counsel for the applicant has submitted that the applicant had entered into an agreement to sale with the occupier of the land Veer Bahadur on 22/11/2022 for consideration of Rs.10 Lakhs under the impression that the land belongs to him only, however, subsequently, an FIR has been lodged by the complainant on 25/03/2025 alleging that his land, on which, the applicant had already constructed a shed, has been illegally occupied by the applicant.
It is submitted that the applicant has already handed over the possession of the land to the complainant and he is presently lodged in jail since 13/06/2025.
It is submitted that the applicant himself has been cheated by the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:21036 2 MCRC-30768-2025 erstwhile occupier Veer Bahadur.
Hence, it is submitted that the bail application be allowed and the applicant be released on bail.

sentences.text: 5. Counsel for the respondent / State, on the other hand has opposed the prayer and it is submitted that no case for grant of bail is made out.

6. Having considered the rival submissions and on perusal of the case diary, taking note of the fact that the possession of the land has already been given to the complainant and the applicant has also filed on record the sale agreement executed in the year 2022, this Court finds force with the contentions raised by learned counsel for the applicant, and further taking note of the fact that the final conclusion of the trial is likely to take sufficient long time, in the considered opinion of this Court, the applicant's application deserves to be allowed.
7.
Accordingly, without commenting on the merits of the case, the application filed by the applicant is allowed.

The applicant is directed to be released on bail upon furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.25,000/- (rupees twenty five thousand) with one solvent surety of the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court for his/her regular appearance before the trial Court during trial with a condition that he / she shall remain present before the court concerned during trial and shall also abide by the conditions enumerated under Section 437 (3) Criminal Procedure Code, 1973.
Certified copy as per rules.
